To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adaptive time stepping is a valuable tool for the reliable numerical approximation of the time evolution of the Gross Pitaevski equation in the semi classical limit and that locally adaptive time stepping is especially beneficial in situations where a high resolution in space is required.

locally adaptive time splitting schemes with a variable time stepsize are effective for the numerical solution Gross Pitaevksii equations with a mildly varying regular or a sharp Gaussian solution and that the locally adaptive finite difference method is favourable regarding accuracy and reliability when applied to the numerical solution of Gross Pitaevski equations in the semi-classical regime.

adaptive time discretisations are favourable for nonlinear Schrodinger type equations with a defocussing nonlinearity or for Gross Pitaesvskii equations with smooth initial data and small parameter e1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to exploit adaptive space and time techniques for the numerical treatment of low dimensional Gross Pitaevkskii equations.
the numerical solution of Gross Pitaevskiiequations by locally adaptive space and timediscretisations.
the numerical analysis of the adaptive time stepping method in the sense of a posteriori error estimation for nonlinear evolution equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
locally adaptive time discretisation schemes are favourable for the numerical solution Gross Pitaevskiiequations in the semi-classical regime.
adaptive space and time methods are beneficial in the numerical solution of Gross Pitaevsky equations.

locally adaptive time splitting schemes with embedded splitting pairs or locally adaptive space discretisations based on finite elements are effective in different situations and can be recommended for the numerical solution Gross Pitaevskiiequations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adaptive time discretisations are beneficial for the numerical treatment of Gross Pitaevsky equations.

the adaptive time splitting scheme is an effective tool for the reliable computation of Gross Pitaevski equations in the semiclassical limit, in particular when the numerical solution is of interest in the entire time interval of interest.

adaptive space and time splitting schemes are a powerful tool for the numerical treatment of nonlinear Schrodiger equations with a defocussing nonlinearity or in the semi classical limit, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adaptive time stepping schemes are effective in different situations.
the adaptive discretisation of nonlinear Schrodiger equations is a promising approach to improve the reliability and accuracy of numerical computations.
adaptive discretisations can be a powerful tool to enhance the reliability of numerical simulations for Gross Pitaeskii equations.
